skills.name: compute_intersection_number_in_chow_ring
skills.description: Calculate the intersection product of divisor classes in the Chow ring of a product of projective spaces to obtain an enumerative integer.
skills.preconditions: A projective variety expressed as a product of projective spaces with known divisor class relations; cycles to intersect are represented by classes in the Chow ring.
skills.postconditions: An integer equal to the degree of the zero‑dimensional cycle representing the intersection.
skills.example: In \(\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1\), intersect the divisor class \(\mathcal{O}(1,0)\) with \(\mathcal{O}(0,1)\); the Chow ring computation yields the number one, reflecting that a horizontal line meets a vertical line in a single point.

skills.name: apply_bertini_smoothness
skills.description: Use Bertini's theorem to guarantee that a general member of a base‑point‑free linear system is smooth.
skills.preconditions: A base‑point‑free linear system on a smooth variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero (or sufficiently large characteristic).
skills.postconditions: Existence of a smooth divisor representing a generic element of the linear system.
skills.example: On a smooth quadric surface, the linear system of hyperplane sections is base‑point‑free; Bertini implies a general hyperplane section is a smooth curve of genus zero.

skills.name: use_frobenius_trace_formula
skills.description: Apply the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula to express the number of rational points over a finite field in terms of the trace of Frobenius on étale cohomology.
skills.preconditions: A proper variety defined over a finite field.
skills.example: For a smooth projective curve of genus one, the trace formula relates \(\#C(\mathbb{F}_q)\) to the eigenvalues of Frobenius on its first cohomology group.

skills.name: estimate_point_counts_via_weil_bounds
skills.description: Use the Weil conjectures to bound the deviation of point counts from the expected main term given by the dimension of the variety.
skills.preconditions: A smooth projective variety over a finite field with known Betti numbers.
skills.postconditions: Inequalities of the form \(|\#X(\mathbb{F}_q)-q^{\dim X}| \leq C\,q^{\dim X-1/2}\) where \(C\) depends on the Betti numbers.
skills.example: For a smooth surface, the bound \(|\#S(\mathbb{F}_q)-q^2| \leq (b_1+2b_2)q^{3/2}\) follows from the Weil estimates.

skills.name: compute_degree_of_finite_etale_map
skills.description: Determine the degree of a finite étale morphism by counting points in a geometric fiber.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism between integral schemes, with at least one geometric point of the target where the fiber is known.
skills.postconditions: An integer equal to the number of points in any geometric fiber, i.e., the degree of the covering.
skills.example: The map \(\mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{A}^1\) given by \(t \mapsto t^2\) is finite étale over the complement of the origin; each fiber consists of two points, so the degree is two.

skills.name: use_chebotarev_density_for_fiber_statistics
skills.description: Apply Chebotarev density to relate the average size of fibers over rational points of varying finite fields to the degree of a finite étale cover.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale cover defined over the integers, and a family of finite fields of increasing size.
skills.postconditions: The limit of the average fiber cardinality equals the degree of the cover.
skills.example: For the cover \(\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathbb{G}_m\) given by \(x \mapsto x^n\), Chebotarev implies that the average number of \(n\)th roots of a random element in \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\) tends to \(n\) as \(p\) grows.

skills.name: apply_hilbert_scheme_parameterization
skills.description: Construct the Hilbert scheme to parametrize subschemes of projective space with a fixed Hilbert polynomial.
skills.preconditions: A projective space and a prescribed Hilbert polynomial.
skills.postconditions: A projective scheme representing the functor of families of subschemes with that Hilbert polynomial.
skills.example: The Hilbert scheme of points of length three in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) is a smooth six‑dimensional variety parametrizing zero‑dimensional subschemes of degree three.

skills.name: use_deformation_to_generic_fiber
skills.description: Transfer enumerative information from the generic fiber of a flat family to special fibers by deformation invariance.
skills.preconditions: A flat family over an irreducible base with a known count on the generic fiber.
skills.postconditions: The same count holds for every fiber, provided the conditions defining the count vary continuously in the family.
skills.example: A family of plane curves of degree three degenerating to a union of a line and a conic preserves the number of inflection points, which is nine on the smooth generic fiber.

skills.name: perform_inclusion_exclusion_on_incidence_conditions
skills.description: Count objects satisfying several incidence conditions by applying the inclusion–exclusion principle to the corresponding subsets.
skills.preconditions: Finite sets of objects and a collection of incidence conditions whose intersections can be enumerated.
skills.postconditions: An integer equal to the number of objects meeting all conditions simultaneously.
skills.example: To count lines in \(\mathbb{P}^3\) meeting two given skew lines, apply inclusion–exclusion to the sets of lines meeting each line individually and their intersection.

skills.name: apply_monodromy_transitivity_to_irreducibility
skills.description: Use the transitivity of the monodromy group on the fibers of a family to deduce that the covering is irreducible.
skills.preconditions: A connected base, a finite étale cover, and a monodromy action that is transitive on a generic fiber.
skills.postconditions: The total space of the cover is irreducible (or geometrically connected).
skills.example: For the family of square roots of a generic polynomial, the Galois group acts transitively on the two roots, implying the corresponding double cover of the parameter space is irreducible.
